newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania aims to be in first wave of EU growth.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania aims to be in first wave of EU growth.

text.p: The Baltic state of Lithuania is aiming to be among the first to join the European Union when it eventually expands, President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Tuesday.

In his annual state-of-the-nation speech to parliament, Brazauskas said Lithuania was also determined to join NATO although huge neighbour Russia is opposed to any of the Balts becoming a member of the military alliance.
"We endorse the proposal to start negotiations with all (EU) candidates at the same time and we shall seek to complete negotiations with the first candidates," Brazauskas said.
Lithuania, for 50 years an unwilling member of the former Soviet Union, set its sights on boosting links with the West after it regained independence six years ago.
It has signed an association agreement with the EU and is one of the few former Communist states formally to apply for full NATO membership.
"Lithuania is prepared to start European Union accession negotiations and supports the idea of setting the negotiation timetable at the coming Amsterdam EU summit in June," he added.
EU leaders are to meet in the Dutch capital on June 16-17 and are expected to discuss a range of subjects, including enlargement.
Brazauskas is a non-executive president but he plays a key role in forming and promoting foreign policy goals.
"Another major issue of foreign policy is integration with NATO in close cooperation with members of the alliance, Poland, other central European and Baltic states," Brazauskas said.
Russia is strongly opposed to any of the Baltic states becoming members of NATO.
But all three small nations see the alliance as the only way to make sure they are never again subject to the domination of Moscow or other large neighbours.
Brazauskas said Lithuania would continue to make sure its relations with Moscow were based on mutual understanding and benefit.
